note: From an OpenStreetMap export (tools/osm-to-kit.mjs, 8 October 2026): the platform lengths, the Heaton Moor Road bridge over the line at the south end, and the Station Store beside it. Side platforms stand 1.68 m outside the slow lines, the tracks at their real spacing; the cutting walls are low brick walls at the cutting's foot, and the terrain's retaining wall rises from their backs to the ground's real height (the Environment Agency's LIDAR: about 7.5 m by the bridge, 4 to 5 m at the north end). Positive v is east. Photos (geograph 7949299 Stephen McKay 2024, 4005063, 4005068, 4005098 and 4005107 El Pollock 2014, 4547160, 4549149 and 4549166 Gerald England 2015, 1508237 England 2009, 3172345 David Dixon 2012, 4886394 2016; Commons 'HeatonChapel Railway4490.JPG'): the Heaton Moor Road bridge is dark brick on segmental arches, drawn as one arch over each pair of tracks on a pier between them, thinner than the real piers, and a smaller arch at the west end that the platform's ramp runs under to Tatton Road South (the way across: there is no footbridge; passengers cross on the road bridge). The booking office is a two-storey Victorian brick building with a hipped slate roof at road level by the bridge, at the south end of the west platform (a newsagent in it); on the east platform a Victorian brick building steps up against the cutting from the platform to the road by the bridge, the stairs inside it (with the way across and the second platform), and runs on north (with the booking office). One curved-roofed canopy on blue posts a platform, drawn as barrel-roofed shelters. The lifts are the game's (there are none). No photo shows a station car park, only cars on the side street, so there is none (OpenStreetMap's car park beside Heaton Moor Road is the medical centre's). OpenStreetMap (main API, 14 October 2026) has no taxi rank: the game's stands on Tatton Road North at the top of the cutting by the booking office; the replacement buses use stop F on Heaton Moor Road south-west of the bridge; short streets join the bridge's ends to Heaton Moor Road, painted on the ground either side. Departure boards on each platform and by the booking office; Sheffield stands by the barriers with the way across (from memory). Its booking office's roof is hipped (the `hipped` part, 12 October 2026, from the photos in this note; the pitch from memory). Across the line at real scale since 13 October 2026 (it was 1.25 times).
